lookahead.why: Truncate the series; every already-closed trade must be identical. This is the test that would have caught the three look-aheads that killed every crypto result in the project.

degenerate.why: Zero-volume bars, flat OHLC, zero sigma, one bar, empty series. Both 2026-09-07 bugs were degenerate-input bugs.

costs.why: Profit factor must fall as cost rises, and R must be affine in the cost multiple - the identity every MEASURED-cost board number uses.

golden.why: A pinned trade list. Any kernel edit that moves a trade has to be explained in the commit rather than discovered weeks later.

second_engine.why: Trade-by-trade agreement with NautilusTrader. An event-driven engine holds no array it could index into, so it cannot reproduce a look-ahead. This is the check that has actually found bugs.

manifest.why: Everything this result depends on is declared, so the stale flag can see it. An undeclared kernel never trips the flag.

fingerprint.why: The board record carries a fingerprint and it still matches the files on disk.

parity.why: Ribbon's twenty moving averages recomputed the slow literal way from the Pine source. Existed for weeks as a SCRIPT that pytest never collected, so nothing ran it.

paired_null.why: The identical search run on phase-randomised data must find LESS than the real market did. Twelve hypotheses have died to this and one (H-005) cleared the gate 1,702 times against its null's 19,062.
